SPECIAL EDITION REQUEST: Home cybersecurity — the ultra deep dive for a HOME environment, scoped to a household running Windows 11 desktops, WSL2 Ubuntu on those machines, and macOS laptops (no enterprise fleet, no corporate MDM). DEFENSIVE ONLY — hardening, hygiene and recovery; not offensive tooling. Wanted: the honest threat model for a home user in 2026 (who actually attacks home machines, and how); platform-by-platform hardening that is real and current — Windows 11 (Defender vs paid AV honestly, BitLocker, Smart App Control, standard-vs-admin accounts), the WSL2 seam specifically (what WSL does and does not isolate, Windows/Linux file-permission crossover, Docker Desktop exposure, dev-machine supply-chain risk from npm/pip/VS Code extensions), and macOS (Gatekeeper/XProtect reality, FileVault, TCC permissions); the home NETWORK layer (router firmware, DNS filtering, IoT/VLAN segmentation, Tailscale-style overlays vs port-forwarding); identity as the real perimeter (passkeys vs TOTP vs SMS, password managers compared honestly post-LastPass, phishing that defeats MFA); backups as the last line (3-2-1, ransomware-proof versioning, actually testing restores); the family angle (protecting a household incl. a tween's devices without surveillance theatre); the community read (r/cybersecurity, r/homelab, security YouTube, what practitioners run at home vs what they tell clients); the sceptic desk — which paid security products are theatre for a home user; and the fresh-peg sweep of 2026 home-relevant incidents/CVEs. (desk: reader direct request via Claude session)

SPECIAL EDITION REQUEST: Da Lat, Vietnam — the ultra deep dive. IMPORTANT CONTEXT: today's No. 73 Travel Desk already ran Da Lat as its two-page Grand Tour (reader-pinned) — this special must go DEEPER and COMPLEMENT it, not re-survey: read No. 73's Travel Desk first and build past it. The full 24pp treatment of the Central Highlands hill station: the deep history (the French hill-station founding, Yersin, the Cité-Jardin plan, the villas and their decay/restoration economics, the Bao Dai summer palace era, the wartime neutrality legend); the coffee economy done properly (Vietnam as the world's robusta giant vs Da Lat's arabica exception, Cau Dat's farms, the specialty wave and its farms/roasters/cafes by name with prices, weasel-coffee ethics honestly); the flower-and-farm industrial belt (Hasfarm, the greenhouse sprawl's environmental cost — honest about the plastic-roof landscape and flooding); the railway story (the Cremaillere rack railway, the restored Da Lat–Trai Mat segment, revival plans); food as its own desk (banh trang nuong, artichoke everything, avocado ice cream, the night market, strawberry/dau tay culture, the best actual addresses); where to actually stay (Ana Mandara villas, the colonial-villa hotels, homestay culture, price tiers); itineraries by trip-length ex-Singapore incl. the SGN connection reality and the Lien Khuong airport upgrade status; adventure honestly age-gated (canyoning safety record with the documented fatalities, waterfalls, the alpine coaster); the pop-culture/K-drama and domestic-tourism boom angle (why young Vietnamese and Koreans flock there); climate as the product (the eternal-spring data vs Singapore's heat, wet/dry season honesty for planning); and the sceptic desk — overtourism, greenhouse sprawl, weekend crowds from HCMC, and whether the romance survives the reality. Community read: r/VietnamTravel, TripAdvisor, Vietnam Coracle, Foody, Vietnamese-language sentiment characterised. (desk: reader direct request via Claude session)

SPECIAL EDITION REQUEST: The Slim d'Hermes Neo Brandebourgs Tourbillon — a single-watch ultra deep dive. PRIMARY SUBJECT, exhausted first: everything verifiable about this specific watch — the release (when, where unveiled, which collection cycle), full specifications (case metal/diameter/thickness, dial craft and the Brandebourg motif's meaning in the Hermes design language and its couture/frogging origin), the MOVEMENT (calibre designation, who designed and manufactures it — the Vaucher/Hermes relationship and Hermes's stake, tourbillon architecture, finishing, power reserve), price and production numbers/limitation, availability and waitlist reality, every serious review and hands-on (Hodinkee, Fratello, Revolution, SJX, Monochrome, WatchesbySJX, Deployant — SJX and Deployant are Singapore-based, note it), collector-forum sentiment (WatchUSeek, r/Watches, Instagram watch-community read), auction/secondary-market presence if any, and how it sits against peer haute-horlogerie tourbillons at its price. HONESTY LAW APPLIES HARD: this is a niche subject — hold or drop what cannot be verified, flag single-source claims in print, never invent a spec, price or quote. IF the single watch cannot honestly fill the book, widen in CONCENTRIC RINGS while keeping the Neo Brandebourgs as the spine: ring 2 = the Slim d'Hermes line (Philippe Delhotal's design era, the Philippe Apeloig typeface story, the ultra-thin micro-rotor calibres, the line's other metiers-d'art and complication pieces); ring 3 = Hermes watchmaking whole — La Montre Hermes history, the Vaucher Manufacture Fleurier stake, dial/case/strap ateliers, the playful-complication canon (Le Temps Suspendu, L'Heure De La Lune, Duc Attele minute-repeater tourbillon), and the collector debate 'is Hermes a real watchmaker?' answered with evidence not vibes; the reader is a serious mechanical-watch collector — write to that level, movement architecture and finishing vocabulary welcome. (desk: reader direct request via Claude session)

SPECIAL EDITION REQUEST: The Hermes Kelly bag — the ultra deep dive. AUDIENCE NOTE, load-bearing: this issue is being made to share with a SERIOUS KELLY COLLECTOR (a friend of the reader). Pitch it at collector level — she already knows what a Kelly is; do NOT write a beginner's explainer or a listicle. She should finish it having learned something she did not know, and should not catch a single error. Depth targets: (1) THE OBJECT'S HISTORY done properly — the 1892 Haut a Courroies saddle origin, the 1930s Sac a Depeches, the 1956 Grace Kelly moment and the 1977 renaming, with dates verified not repeated from blogs. (2) HOW IT IS ACTUALLY MADE — one artisan per bag start to finish, the saddle stitch with two needles and waxed linen thread, hours per bag (verify the real figure, do not repeat marketing rounding), the Hermes ecole de maroquinerie and the leather-workers' training pipeline, the ateliers and the production-capacity story. (3) THE LEATHER SCHOOL — Togo, Epsom, Box calf, Chevre Mysore, Barenia, Swift, Clemence: grain, scratch behaviour, structure, patina and which suits which size/style, plus exotics (alligator/croc/lizard, the CITES reality and the lumiere/matte distinction). (4) THE TAXONOMY collectors argue about — Sellier vs Retourne, sizes 25/28/32/35 and the Mini Kelly II 20, Kelly Pochette, Kelly Danse/Elan/Cut/Doll and the special orders (HSS horseshoe stamp), hardware palladium vs gold, stamping/date codes and the 2021 system change. (5) THE ACQUISITION GAME told HONESTLY — the quota-bag reality, pre-spend expectations, SA relationships, why boutiques deny a wishlist exists, and the 2024 US antitrust class action over tying; the resale ecosystem (Privé Porter, Bagista, the SG scene) with real premium ranges. (6) THE MARKET — auction records at Sotheby's/Christie's incl. the 2025 record-setting sales, the Himalaya benchmark, and an HONEST examination of the 'better than gold' appreciation claim (which studies actually say what, what survivorship bias hides). (7) CARE, RESTORATION AND AUTHENTICATION — the Hermes spa service and its wait times/limits, what they will and will not restore, and the authentication tells collectors actually use (stitch angle, stamp fonts, hardware weight) without writing a counterfeiter's manual. (8) THE COMMUNITY read — PurseForum's Hermes sub-forums, r/TheHermesGame, the YouTube/IG collector voices — attributed, never invented. (9) SINGAPORE angle: the Liat Towers boutique, local reseller scene, and humidity/tropical care for leather. (10) THE SCEPTIC, mandatory: the quota game's real cost, whether a Kelly is an investment or a beautiful consumable, and the ethics questions collectors themselves raise (exotics, the artificial-scarcity critique). HONESTY LAW IN FULL: never invent a price, date, hours figure, or quote; flag single-sourced claims in print; hold what cannot be verified. (desk: reader direct request via Claude session)

SPECIAL EDITION REQUEST: Vietnamese women working in Singapore's KTV lounges — a serious social-affairs ultra deep dive. THE SUBJECT IS THE WOMEN AND THE SYSTEM AROUND THEM, reported with dignity: a labour-migration story about money, law, risk and stigma. EDITORIAL GUARDRAILS, non-negotiable (same standard as No. 63's S&M descent: culture-focused, non-explicit): this is NOT a consumer guide — no venue recommendations or 'where to go', no prices for sexual services, no procurement detail, no reproduction of individual women's photos, working names or forum 'reviews' of specific people, nothing titillating. Forums (Sammyboy/SBF, HardwareZone EDMW) are to be mined as DEMAND-SIDE and industry-mechanics EVIDENCE and read critically — they are punter boards, so treat them as an artifact revealing the customers, the market's structure and its attitudes; quote sparingly and analytically, never as endorsement. COVER: (1) THE PIPELINE — recruitment in Vietnam (which provinces, brokers/agents, the fees and debt structure, what women are told vs what they find), and the visa machinery that makes it work: Social Visit Pass cycling, Work Permits, and especially the Performing Artiste Card regime and its history. (2) THE WORK ITSELF — what a KTV hostess job actually is (lady drinks, commission, sitting fees, tips, hours), the tiered venues, and the honest legal grey zone of where it does and does not cross into commercial sex. (3) THE MONEY — earnings ranges (attributed/held, never invented), commission structures, remittances home and what they fund. (4) THE LAW — public entertainment licensing, the Employment of Foreign Manpower Act, immigration offences, vice-raid enforcement patterns, the Prevention of Human Trafficking Act 2014 and its ACTUAL prosecution/conviction record (low — say so plainly), and what happens to women when a place is raided: detention, deportation, and how the victim-versus-offender determination is made. (5) THE JULY 2021 KTV COVID CLUSTER — the national story that exposed the industry's scale, the policy response, and the xenophobic backlash aimed specifically at Vietnamese women; report the backlash as a fact about Singapore, evenhandedly. (6) TRAFFICKING VS AGENCY, the hard part done with real nuance — the spectrum from voluntary economic migration through deception to debt bondage; steel-man BOTH the trafficking framing and the migrant-agency/sex-worker-rights framing (Project X's position that conflating the two harms workers deserves its full weight, as does the evidence of genuine coercion). Sallie Yea's academic work on Vietnamese women in Singapore's entertainment sector is a key source. (7) SUPPORT AND COMMUNITY — HOME, Project X, AWARE, Vietnamese diaspora networks, embassy/consular reality. (8) THE VIETNAM SIDE — Vietnamese-language reporting on recruitment and the sending villages, the returnee experience and stigma at home. (9) THE SCEPTIC — what the data genuinely supports versus moral panic in both directions; numbers here are scarce, contested and often come from advocacy or enforcement sources with incentives, so name the incentive whenever citing one. HONESTY LAW AT MAXIMUM: never invent a statistic, a price, a case or a quotation — and above all DO NOT FABRICATE FIRST-PERSON TESTIMONY from women; if the book quotes a woman, it must be from a published, attributable interview (ST/CNA/Rice Media/academic fieldwork), clearly cited. Flag single-sourced claims; hold what cannot be verified. Sources to work: Straits Times/CNA/TODAY archives, Rice Media, academic literature (Yea et al.), Project X and HOME reports, US State Dept TIP country reports on Singapore, published court judgments, Vietnamese press, and the local forums as critical demand-side artifacts. (desk: reader direct request via Claude session)

SPECIAL EDITION REQUEST: Bangladeshi construction workers in Singapore — a social-affairs ultra deep dive, and the second in the reader's migrant-labour series (after the Vietnamese KTV book). SAME EDITORIAL LAW AS THAT ISSUE: the subject is the MEN AND THE SYSTEM AROUND THEM, reported with dignity and specificity, never as either a pity portrait or a policy brochure. NEVER FABRICATE FIRST-PERSON TESTIMONY — every quotation from a worker must come from a published, attributable source (TWC2 case notes, ST/CNA/TODAY/Rice Media interviews, academic fieldwork, or the workers' OWN published writing) with a citation. Invent no statistic, fee, wage or case; name the incentive behind advocacy, employer or government figures alike; flag single-sourced claims; hold what cannot be verified. THE READER SPECIFICALLY WANTS THE ORIGIN-COUNTRY LENS WORKED HARD — Bangladeshi press and forums are a primary source, not a footnote: Prothom Alo (Bengali), The Daily Star, New Age, Dhaka Tribune, bdnews24, The Business Standard on recruitment abuse, BMET policy and remittance data; Bengali-language Facebook groups and YouTube/TikTok vlogs made BY workers bound for or living in Singapore; and the instructive gap between how the Bangladeshi press covers Singapore and how Singapore covers Bangladeshis. Mark translated material as translated. COVER: (1) THE PIPELINE — the dalal/broker network in the sending districts (Tangail, Comilla, Brahmanbaria, Munshiganj, Narsingdi), BMET registration and the licensed-agency system, the medical and skills-test gauntlet, and above all THE FEE: Bangladeshi workers pay among the world's highest recruitment costs (report the real range with sources), and how families finance it — land sales, mortgages, moneylenders, microloans. (2) THE DEBT ARC — how many months or years to clear it, what happens to a man repatriated before he does, and how that sunk cost quietly disciplines a workforce into accepting conditions. (3) THE WORK — the Work Permit regime and employer-tied status, SEC(K)/skills certification, the construction sector's reliance, wages honestly (basic vs overtime, what actually reaches the bank), and the levy/quota machinery. (4) LIVING — dormitories: the pre-2020 reality, the April 2020 COVID outbreak that put a six-figure workforce into the national story (S11 Punggol; the share of Singapore's cases), the reforms that followed (new dormitory standards, PBD requirements) and an HONEST assessment of what materially changed versus what was announced. (5) INJURY, WAGES AND DEATH — WICA claims, TADM mediation, TWC2's own caseload evidence, the repatriation-before-claim problem, and workplace fatality/injury statistics from MOM with the definitional caveats stated. (6) THE MONEY HOME — remittances as one of Bangladesh's largest foreign-exchange earners, formal channels vs hundi, what the money actually builds in a village, and the social status of the 'probashi'. (7) THE CULTURE, and give it real space — this is the chapter that makes the book sing: Banglar Kantha, the Bengali-language newspaper published in Singapore; the Migrant Worker Poetry Competition and the worker-poet movement (Md Mukul Hossine's 'Me Migrant', Zakir Hossain Khokan's work, One Bag One Book); migrant photography and vlogging; cricket, Little India on a Sunday, the food and phone-shop economy that grew around them. Quote the poets properly and by name — published work, cited. (8) THE 2013 LITTLE INDIA RIOT and its long policy shadow. (9) ADVOCACY AND ITS ARGUMENTS — TWC2, HOME, MWC, ItsRainingRaincoats; where they agree, where they genuinely disagree, and MOM's position given its full steel-man rather than a strawman. (10) THE SCEPTIC, mandatory: what actually improved post-COVID versus what was communications; the recruitment-fee problem Singapore has not solved because the fees are charged in Bangladesh, outside its jurisdiction; and the honest tension between a construction cost base, a housing programme, and what the men are paid. Singapore reader, so make the read-through concrete: the flats and MRT lines this labour built. (desk: reader direct request via Claude session)
